objective_ids.LO1: Compare intervention, specimen, timepoint, and phenotype representation across the two studies.
objective_ids.LO2: Explain how design, provenance, and platform constrain cross-study conclusions.
objective_ids.LO3: Apply and document a RefMet-centered metabolite and metadata harmonization workflow.
objective_ids.LO4: Retrieve, analyze, and interpret public Metabolomics Workbench data within study-design boundaries.
objective_ids.LO5: Evaluate access patterns and adapt the workflow to another resource.

items.prompt: Two studies report a RefMet match for the same metabolite. Which conclusion is justified?

options.A: Their quantitative values may be concatenated without further checks.
options.B: Their submitted labels have a shared standardized-name candidate; analytical specificity and context still require review.
options.C: The metabolite was confirmed by an authentic standard in both studies.

items.rationale: RefMet supplies a nomenclature bridge. It does not establish experimental identification level, matrix equivalence, common scale, or biological causation.

items.prompt: Which evidence establishes the access pattern for a candidate dataset?

options.A: The reputation of the research consortium.
options.B: The access tier remembered from a prior release.
options.C: Current first-party documentation and a dated check of the exact dataset and intended action.
options.D: The fact that a publication cites the dataset.

items.rationale: Access is specific to a dataset, release, action, user, and current policy. Program reputation or historical status is insufficient evidence.

items.prompt: When phenotype anchor and study are perfectly confounded, what is the safest interpretation of a PCA separation between studies?

options.A: It proves diet and exercise have different metabolic effects.
options.B: It proves the exercise cohort is more heterogeneous.
options.C: It is exploratory separation that may reflect biological, technical, or design differences that cannot be uniquely attributed.

items.rationale: Study, phenotype, matrix, platform, laboratory, and population differences are not separable in a two-study contrast. PCA does not resolve that confounding.

items.prompt: One study records fasting duration in hours and another records only yes/no fasting status. For a binary fasted-versus-not-fasted description, how should the fields be classified?

options.B: Partially comparable after a documented derivation and loss of detail.
options.D: Directly comparable for modeling fasting duration.

items.rationale: The hourly field can be collapsed to a binary construct if the threshold is justified, but the finer information is lost and duration cannot be modeled across both studies.

items.prompt: What is the best evidence that rows at several timepoints come from the same participant?

options.C: A documented subject-sample relationship in the deposited metadata.
options.D: The word longitudinal in the publication title.

items.rationale: Repeated-measures linkage needs explicit study metadata or a documented and validated parsing rule. Similarity, ordering, or a title is indirect evidence.

items.prompt: Why is post insufficient as a harmonized timepoint?

options.B: It lacks an intervention anchor, offset, and physiological state.

items.rationale: A timepoint needs a defined anchor and interval. In this module, diet-study days and acute exercise recovery labels represent different processes.

items.prompt: A fuzzy RefMet lookup returns two plausible candidates and the deposited record has no formula or external identifier. What should you do?

options.B: Select whichever candidate appears in the other study.
options.C: Mark the row review_required or unmapped, preserve both candidates, and exclude it from exact overlap until resolved.
options.D: Replace it with a chemical class label and call it exact.

items.rationale: The available evidence does not support a unique mapping. Preserving uncertainty prevents a forced match from inflating overlap.

items.prompt: When can umol/L be converted to mmol/L for cross-study comparison?

options.A: Whenever both unit strings are present.
options.B: Only after confirming the same quantity, compatible matrix and denominator, quantification basis, and a recorded conversion.

items.rationale: Dimensional convertibility is necessary but not sufficient. Matrix, analyte, denominator, calibration, and quantification basis must also support the comparison.

items.prompt: Which crosswalk design is most reproducible?

options.A: One column containing the final clean name.
options.B: Original and standardized names, source and query provenance, mapping status, evidence, reviewer, decision reason, and purpose-specific eligibility.
options.C: A list containing only mapped analytes.
options.D: A table in which all ambiguities are manually forced to one value.

items.rationale: A reproducible crosswalk preserves source identity, evidence, decisions, uncertainty, and the purpose for which a row is eligible.

items.prompt: Why should the QPP rows in ST001521 not be included in biological PCA?

options.A: They are pooled quality-control samples rather than participant-timepoint observations.
options.D: Quality-control samples must always be deleted from the repository.

items.rationale: Pooled QC samples can be useful for analytical diagnostics, but they do not represent independent participant-timepoint observations and should not drive biological inference.

items.prompt: What does the intermediate overlap of 153 represent?

options.A: 153 metabolites proven to respond to both diet and exercise.
options.B: 153 shared nonblank exact RefMet strings before artifact and eligibility exclusions under a specific build.

items.rationale: The raw string intersection is a reproducibility checkpoint. Eight isotope/internal-standard rows in ST003348 map to ordinary names and are excluded in the conservative biological set, leaving 145 in the audited build.

options.A: A separate within-study PCA is an exploratory view whose pattern must be interpreted with preprocessing, repeated measures, and design context.
options.B: Separation between the two studies proves a diet-versus-exercise mechanism.

items.rationale: PCA is exploratory and preprocessing-sensitive. Separate within-study models preserve design context but still do not prove causal mechanisms.

items.prompt: What is the most accurate access description for MoTrPAC?

options.B: Every MoTrPAC dataset is fully open.
options.C: Access is dataset- and release-dependent; public and restricted paths exist and must be verified.
options.D: MoTrPAC data can be used only inside All of Us.

items.rationale: Current first-party documentation describes public releases accessible without login and restricted or embargoed data with additional requirements.

items.prompt: What should move into a controlled-compute environment?

options.A: Approved analysis code and public reference resources that comply with environment policy.
options.B: A public link that silently downloads participant data to a local laptop.
options.D: A module cache populated with participant-level records.

items.rationale: Portable code and permitted reference resources can move into the governed workspace; controlled participant-level data remain in approved storage and credentials are never embedded.

items.prompt: A dataset is publicly downloadable and scientifically incompatible with your target estimand. What is the correct decision?

options.A: Pool it because access is open.
options.B: Treat access and scientific compatibility separately; revise or stop the integration.
options.C: Standardize names and ignore the design.

items.rationale: A dataset can be open and still be unsuitable for the intended comparison. Check access and scientific fit separately.
